daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Political debate intensified around proposed changes to presidential nomination requirements, with Hanura criticizing a proposal that presidential candidates be supported by at least two parliamentary factions, calling the idea an "unintelligent whisper." The party's objection highlights coalition sensitivities as discussion also emerged about separating presidential and legislative elections, drawing mixed responses from DPR members and political parties. These debates come as the political system continues to grapple with electoral reform questions.

  • The Constitutional Court heard challenges to Vice President Gibran's educational qualifications, with lawyer Denny Indrayana stating there is no proof Gibran graduated from senior high school, while former President Jokowi responded to the lawsuit over educational requirements and one lawyer provocatively said "I will kiss the feet" of anyone who can produce Jokowi's original diploma in court.
  • Former Minister of Religious Affairs Yaqut drew criticism for pushing through a 50:50 hajj quota by invoking Jokowi's name while ignoring DPR agreements, with a former director general describing it as "a kick without a shadow" maneuver.
  • Prosecutors at the corruption trial of former Ombudsman chairman demanded 5.5 years imprisonment for Hery Susanto, who is preparing his defense.
  • The Attorney General reshuffled 16 officials, replacing 10 district attorney heads.
  • Justice Minister Yusril vowed sanctions for Cibinong prison staff if proven to have commercialized facilities, amid revelations of luxury cell clusters and alleged extortion at the facility holding high-profile inmates including Ferdy Sambo, though the West Java corrections office denied special facilities existed for Sambo.
  • A DPR member called on the government to pay attention to the fate of private school teachers.
  • Advocacy groups urged that the Statistics Bill not restrict surveys through licensing requirements.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia formally received the Italian-built KRI Sriwijaya-100 frigate, with the red-and-white flag replacing the Italian banner on the vessel. However, the TNI Navy disclosed that NATO communication systems were not included in the grant and will be replaced with Indonesian versions. The transfer represents a significant addition to Indonesia's naval capabilities.

  • Indonesia's delegation walked out at the UN when Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu was scheduled to speak, while separately calling for peace and recovery for the people of Gaza.
  • Indonesia called for protection of humanitarian personnel in conflict zones at a UN forum.
  • Indonesia urged global solidarity to realize the right to development at an international gathering.
  • Indonesia and Russia explored cooperation in satellite technology and AI development.
  • The Indonesian embassy in Muscat facilitated promotion of Indonesia's health sector at the 2026 Oman Health Exhibition.

Other

The appeal court reduced former Education Minister Nadiem Makarim's sentence to nine years in the Chromebook corruption case, down from his original conviction. Nadiem bowed his head as he listened to the verdict. The high-profile case has drawn sustained public attention to corruption in education procurement.

  • The DPR Budget Committee calculated the cost of free education at Rp302 trillion.
  • President Prabowo ordered scientists and villagers be involved in the reconstituted peatland agency to strengthen forest fire prevention.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs expressed regret over a book titled "Hunting Muhammad," saying it has potential to cause unrest.
  • Two new islands formed near Mount Anak Krakatau following recent eruptions.
  • Indonesia is hosting the 2026 World Islamic Tourism Forum to strengthen access to global tourism markets, while preparations are underway for an international imam conference.
  • Indonesia boosted health preparedness as El Niño is forecast to persist into 2027, while one million West Java residents are affected by drought with disaster authorities sending 27 million liters of water aid.
